name: agent-fs-write-operations
body:
Code-writer implementer agents must be able to delete, move, and copy files inside the surface they own, so a plan task with a `deletes` / `renames` / `moves` verb is implementable. Today they cannot: the generated implementers carry only shallow bash grants (the core implementer has `rm src/*.rs`; each frontend implementer has one or two `rm <dir>/*.<ext>` patterns) and no `mv` or `cp` at all, so a plan `deletes`/`renames` task is unimplementable.

The capability is delivered by a small suite of filesystem tools — `apg_rm`, `apg_mv`, `apg_cp` — installed by `apg init`, whose path argument is scoped by the SAME per-path glob permission mechanism as `edit`, mirrored under `apg/.worktrees/*/` per the agent-builder's rule 10. This is a scoped capability, never a blanket grant: a path outside the agent's granted globs is refused, and an operation may not cross the caller's project/worktree boundary. The suite tools replace the shallow bash `rm <dir>/*.<ext>` grants.

Scope: rm + mv + cp only. The change-set edits `opencode-suite/**` product source (the new tool files, the shared `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` plumbing, and the `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` template) plus the binary's install registry (`rust.apg.install`'s `SUITE_TOOLS`). It does NOT edit the repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` (consumer artifacts refreshed out-of-band with the installed release). Plain filesystem operations only — no `git rm`/`git mv` — and no change to the binary's node/edge mutation surface (`apg node rm` / `apg edge rm` mutate graph nodes, not files).

Acceptance criteria:
- `apg init` installs the three tools into `~/.opencode/tools/`: `rust.apg.install`'s `SUITE_TOOLS` carries one entry per new tool.
- A generated implementer agent is granted `apg_rm`/`apg_mv`/`apg_cp` scoped to exactly its owned path globs (and the same globs under `apg/.worktrees/*/`), replacing the shallow bash `rm <dir>/*.<ext>` grants.
- An fs-op whose source path (and, for mv/cp, destination path) is matched by the agent's granted globs succeeds; a path outside them is refused.
- An fs-op whose path escapes the caller's project/worktree boundary is refused.
- The install-assertion e2e (`rust.main_e2e.e2e.suite_installs_node_edge_project_tools_and_retires_spec_invariant`) is extended to assert the three tools are embedded and installed, and stays green.
